title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (built up on the preceding pages). A 1-dimensional 'model of form' is a set L of 'lieux' (points) together with a set S of 'segments'. Each segment I comes with:
- a support Ĩ ⊂ L;
- a boundary ∂I ∈ P_2(L), a 2-element subset of Ĩ;
- an interior Ĩ° = Ĩ \ ∂I.

Previous-page definitions and results.
- A point x is regular if it lies in some Ĩ°. L_r is the union of all Ĩ°, and L_s = L \ L_r is the set of singular points.
- Order of a point: the number of branches at it. Order 1 means an end point ('lieu-bout'), order 0 an isolated point.
- F4 (gluing axiom): two segments meeting exactly in a common regular end point z glue uniquely to a segment with support Ĩ'∪Ĩ'' and boundary {x,y}.
- Cor. 1 (extending a segment past a regular end point): if x ∈ ∂I is regular, there is J with Ĩ ⊂ J̃, x in J̃°, and the other end point y kept.

This page.

Cor. 2: if both end points of I are regular, there is J ∈ S with Ĩ ⊂ J̃°. Proof: apply Cor. 1 twice, once at each end. Any segment whose ends are regular can thus be enlarged so that it lies in the interior of a larger segment.

Axiom F5: the order of a regular point (which is known to be ≥ 2, by the argument of Cor. 1 using F1–F3) is exactly 2. So regular points are locally 'line-like': no branching at an interior point of a segment.

F'5, a reformulation of F5: for x ∈ L_r, the family of open supports Ĩ° (I ∈ S) containing x is a filter base. That is, for I', I'' with x ∈ Ĩ'° ∩ Ĩ''°, there is I with x ∈ Ĩ° ⊂ Ĩ'° ∩ Ĩ''°. A note adds that one may equivalently ask for the closed support Ĩ ⊂ Ĩ'° ∩ Ĩ''°.

This is the familiar fact that, at a point of order 2, the open arcs through x form a neighbourhood base of a 1-manifold point. It is phrased purely in the combinatorial structure (L, S, ~, ∂), with no topology given in advance: the topology on L_r is to be generated by the Ĩ°.

Crossed-out remark: take S_0 ⊂ S, set L' = ∪_{I∈S_0} Ĩ and S' = {I | Ĩ ⊂ L'}, with the induced maps S' → P(L') and S' → P_2(L'). Grothendieck asks whether F1–F5 still hold. The next page answers yes, for an arbitrary subset L' ⊂ L: subobjects are again models of 1-dimensional forms.

Purpose: an axiomatic, point-set-free definition of 1-dimensional 'tame' topological forms (graph-like spaces). It is the first stage of the 1986 programme 'Vers une géométrie des formes', in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: The NB 'x ∈ Ĩ° ⊂ Ĩ'°∩Ĩ''° ⟺ Ĩ ⊂ Ĩ'°∩Ĩ''°' is not literally an equivalence. The right side must also require x ∈ Ĩ°, presumably understood. It also needs the shrink/extend results (Cor. 1/2) to pass between closed and open supports. This is a minor gap.

The equivalence F5 ⟺ F'5 is asserted without proof. It is plausible: at order ≥3, two segments through x using branch pairs (a,b) and (b,c) have open-support intersection lying in branch b ∪ {x}, which contains no segment with x interior. Making it rigorous requires the precise definition of 'order' given earlier, which is not on this page.

The crossed-out remark's question, whether F1–F5 survive restriction to L', is answered affirmatively on the next page without proof. Stability of F4 under restriction depends on the glued support being exactly Ĩ'∪Ĩ'', which the previous page seems to assert ('par égalité').

ideas.what: Cor. 2: a segment with regular end points lies in the interior of a larger segment
ideas.modern_name: extendability of arcs in 1-manifold points; local structure of graphs

ideas.what: Axiom F5 / F'5: regular points have order exactly 2, equivalently open segments through x form a filter base
ideas.modern_name: a regular point of a topological graph is a 1-manifold point; open arcs form a neighbourhood base
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; axiomatic analogues in ordered/betweenness geometry (Pasch, Hilbert, Veblen)

ideas.what: Axiomatic structure (L, S, support, boundary) for 1-dimensional 'forms', stable under restriction to subsets
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial/axiomatic tame topology of dimension 1 (cf. o-minimal 1-dimensional sets, topological graphs, segment/betweenness structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) in outline; o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses 'topologie modérée' only in general terms; these specific axioms are not there to my knowledge

missed.claim: A purely combinatorial axiom system (points + segments with support and boundary, axioms F1–F5) for 1-dimensional tame topological forms, intended as the base case of a 'geometry of forms'. It is not developed in the published tame-topology literature, which went the o-minimal route instead.
missed.quote: F'5) Soit x ∈ L_r, et considérons les Ĩ° (I∈S) tels que x ∈ Ĩ°, ceux-ci forment une base de filtre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an alternative, topology-free foundation for tame 1-dimensional spaces, close to synthetic or betweenness geometry. It could be compared with o-minimal definable curves or with the definition of topological graphs. On its own this page is elementary, though.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (regular points of order 2; the filter-base reformulation; extension of segments; stability under restriction) is elementary and folklore in substance. The interest is only historical: an unpublished attempt at axiomatizing tame 1-dimensional forms from 1986.
transcription_corrections: 'S' → P_r(L')' should read 'S' → P_2(L')' (2-element subsets), consistent with the next page.
'(i.e. tel qu'il est ≥ 2)' is more likely '(on sait qu'il est ≥ 2)', referring to the argument of Cor. 1 that regular points have order ≥ 2.
Left lower margin likely begins 'Axiomes des formes régulières' (or '... des lieux réguliers'), not 'Axiomes de régularité'.
In the NB, the right-hand side should be read as 'Ĩ ⊂ Ĩ'°∩Ĩ''°' with x ∈ Ĩ° implicit.
